spike.notes: Trimmed offline build works with plain g++ in about 10 s: no GN and no network after the clone and the two small submodules. Reference passes 66/66 upstream tests (TestTLV 53, TestTLVVectorWriter 4, TestMessageHeader 9) three times with identical results. The differential corpus (1000 TLV and 1000 header cases) was byte-identical across three runs. Base fails to compile. Harness cost is low, about 1 day. Main risks are Band/K8 (a frontier model may recall Matter TLV) and the scope of about 8000 lines, which is large for a 4-8 h tier, though it gives good partial-credit buckets. Hidden tests would be derived from the gtest-shimmed TestTLV.

full_card.band: Budget tier 8 h. Frontier estimate about 6 h for the whole scope, including build wiring. Partial buckets: reader types and containers, writer, tags, error classification, message header. Weaker models fail on error semantics. No dated public evidence, so Band 3.
full_card.build_cost: Unknown: smoke_build is empty (no verdict). Trimmed GN or CMake build of src/lib/core plus MessageHeader needs CHIPError, support headers and possibly nlassert and nlio submodules. Estimate 2 to 4 days of harness work.
full_card.deliverable: C++ TLV reader, writer, utilities and message header encode/decode with the upstream API, built via a trimmed GN or CMake setup.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Base fails to build without the removed headers, so the start scores 0. Close: no TLV library on the image, tests and fuzz targets removed, hidden tests outside /app, no git history, network off at run time. Check that the agent cannot restore the removed files from a build cache or a sibling checkout.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden unit tests derived from TestTLV.cpp (not TestTlv.cpp) plus a differential corpus of random nested structures, malformed input and integer-width boundaries; exact bytes and error codes compared. Size not counted; estimated hundreds to thousands of cases.
full_card.local_fit: gVisor CPU build, 8 cores, 16 GB; no GPU or network needed at run time, provided the trimmed build avoids third-party submodule fetches.
full_card.lookup: direct: the complete removed source is public on GitHub and in third-party mirrors. Offline run and a history-less snapshot close the path, but a frontier model may recall much of the Matter TLV format from the spec.

spike_plan.kill_if: Trimmed build needs network fetches of third-party code that cannot be vendored, or the core files cannot be isolated from the wider support library without more than 5 days of harness work (K12).
spike_plan.pass_if: Trimmed build of the core TLV and MessageHeader files completes offline in under 2 hours of harness work; TestTLV passes deterministically over three runs; corpus is byte-identical across runs; base fails to build.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone project-chip/connectedhomeip at v1.6.1.0 with submodules needed for src/lib/core (nlassert, nlio if required).
Build src/lib/core (TLV files) and src/transport/raw/MessageHeader.cpp with a trimmed CMake or GN target, offline after the fetch; record the time and any missing headers.
Build and run the upstream TestTLV.cpp and TestTLVVectorWriter.cpp; record per-test results for determinism over three runs.
Delete the TLV reader/writer/utilities and MessageHeader files in a copy, confirm the trimmed build fails (base scores 0).

Write a small generator that encodes 1,000 random nested structures and boundary integer widths with the upstream code, and saves the bytes and error codes as the reference corpus; re-run to confirm byte-identical output.
Check that the snapshot build plus the corpus runs without network and within 8 cores and 16 GB.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: connectedhomeip v1.6.1.0 is Apache-2.0 with TLV core in src/lib/core and message header in src/transport/raw, though the seed's names are partly wrong (TestTLV.cpp, not TestTlv.cpp; no message-header test file). Its main risks are the unverified trimmed build (smoke_build is empty) and the direct public lookup, so it is worth the 60-minute spike at an 8 h tier before any build work.

v2.note: Real Apache-2.0 code, the upstream files as reference, and a differential corpus for exact bytes and error codes. Matter TLV is fully specified and close to the publicly documented Weave API, so the 6 h frontier estimate in an 8 h tier carries K8 risk, and the weaker-model gap is unproven. The headers must ship as the API contract. MessageHeader lives in src/transport/raw, and the reference's 3,000 lines are not verified. Isolating a trimmed GN/CMake build from connectedhomeip is the main build cost. Including TLVUpdater, CircularBuffer and VectorWriter would widen the scope.
